title: Multidisciplinary decision-making in the management of recurrent glioblastoma - a multi-centre UK questionnaire study
abstract: Abstract Background Recurrent glioblastoma (GB) carries a poor prognosis, with physical and cognitive decline significantly affecting patients’ survival and quality of life. Unlike newly-diagnosed GB, there is a paucity of level 1 evidence to guide management, including uncertainty regarding the clinical efficacy and cost-effectiveness of repeat resection prior to second-line chemotherapy. We surveyed UK neuro-oncology specialists to evaluate decision-making practices regarding recurrent GB management and the clinical features influencing them. Methods Between December 2023 and April 2024, a 35-item questionnaire was distributed to consultant neuro-oncologists and neuro-oncology surgeons. Respondents were presented with seven case vignettes simulating first GB recurrences and asked to select suitable treatments, including their single preferred option. We also explored which factors routinely influenced decision-making and extent of multi-disciplinary team (MDT) involvement. Results Thirty-eight responses came from 23 consultant neuro-oncology surgeons and 15 consultant neuro-oncologists across 22 NHS hospitals (response rate 73%). Only 71% routinely re-discussed first recurrence at MDT meetings, with higher re-presentation rates among surgeons. Use of advanced imaging to confirm recurrence was variable: MRI perfusion (74%), MR spectroscopy (53%) and no routine advanced imaging (24%). Across seven vignettes, repeat resection followed by second-line chemotherapy was favoured in focally-restricted and late recurrences, but rarely considered for deep-seated or multifocal disease. Second-line chemotherapy was deemed feasible in most scenarios. Re-irradiation was rarely selected, except in late recurrence with good performance status. Best supportive care was often identified as feasible alongside active treatments, particularly with poor prognostic indicators. Factors most commonly influencing re-resection decisions included recurrence interval, performance status, anticipated extent of resection, eloquence and number of tumour foci. Conclusions Substantial inter-clinician variability in preferred management suggests a high degree of clinical equipoise. In this context, there is strong support for randomised trials exploring the clinical efficacy of different management options in recurrent GB, including re- resection surgery.

title: Oral lichen planus in a patient with neurofibromatosis type 1: the first biopsy- confirmed case report
abstract: Abstract Oral lichen planus co-occurring with neurofibromatosis type 1 is exceptionally rare. A comprehensive literature search revealed no prior reports of biopsy-confirmed OLP in NF1 patients. This report describes the first such case in a 22-year-old woman with familial NF1 confirmed by whole exome sequencing (pathogenic variant: c.2850 + 1delG). The patient presented with a 6-month history of intermittent burning and discomfort in the buccal mucosa during orthodontic treatment. Clinical examination showed bilateral reticular white striae with erythematous erosions on the buccal mucosa, alongside classic NF1 features including multiple café-au-lait macules and neurofibromas. Differential diagnoses such as lichenoid reaction to amalgam, systemic lupus erythematosus, and drug-induced lichenoid reaction were excluded based on the absence of any amalgam restorations, negative serological tests for autoimmune markers (including ANA and anti-dsDNA), lack of systemic symptoms suggestive of SLE, and no history of medications associated with lichenoid reactions. The diagnosis of erosive OLP was clinicopathologic, supported by histopathology revealing band-like lymphocytic infiltrate, basal keratinocyte necrosis, and Civatte bodies. Treatment included incisional biopsy and topical triamcinolone acetonide 0.1%, resulting in complete resolution of lesions and symptoms within one month. No recurrence was observed during the 6-month follow-up, and orthodontic treatment progressed uneventfully. This case documents the first biopsy-confirmed erosive OLP in an NF1 patient, emphasizing the importance of routine oral screening and multidisciplinary management given the potential risk of malignant transformation in OLP (approximately 1–2%).

title: Neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio and late gadolinium enhancement in clinically suspected myocarditis: a multicentre retrospective study
abstract: Abstract Background Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging identifies myocardial involvement in myocarditis and carries prognostic weight. The neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio (NPAR) combines neutrophil predominance with serum albumin, a negative acute-phase reactant. Whether NPAR is associated with LGE, and whether it adds information to its individual components and to routinely available clinical data, is unknown. Methods This retrospective observational study included 1,055 adults with clinically suspected myocarditis who underwent CMR at seven tertiary cardiovascular centres in Türkiye between October 2022 and September 2025. All studies were reviewed centrally by three cardiovascular radiologists blinded to clinical and laboratory data (Fleiss' κ = 0.83). Variables significant on univariable analysis (p < 0.10) were entered into multivariable logistic regression models, the shape of the association was examined using restricted cubic splines, and the incremental value of NPAR over the clinical and laboratory model was assessed using discrimination and reclassification metrics. Results LGE was present in 285 patients (27.0%). NPAR was higher in the LGE-positive group [1.65 (1.40–1.92) vs. 1.29 (1.02–1.55); p < 0.001]. In the multivariable model, NPAR remained independently associated with LGE positivity (adjusted odds ratio per 1 standard deviation 4.381, 95% confidence interval 3.248–5.907; p < 0.001), and the Nagelkerke R² rose from 0.157 to 0.387. Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a positive association across the observed range with evidence of non-linearity (p = 0.013). Adding NPAR increased the area under the curve of the model from 0.728 (0.687–0.768) to 0.839 (0.806–0.872) (difference 0.111; p < 0.001), with an integrated discrimination improvement of 0.194 (0.133–0.251) and a continuous net reclassification improvement of 0.843 (0.674–1.011), both p < 0.001. As a single marker, NPAR yielded an area under the curve of 0.750 (0.718–0.782) at a cut-off of 1.43, discriminating LGE better than either constituent (both p < 0.0001). Conclusions In clinically suspected myocarditis, NPAR was independently associated with CMR-defined LGE positivity, discriminated LGE better than either of its own components, and provided significant incremental discrimination and reclassification over a clinical and laboratory model. NPAR may serve as a low-cost adjunctive marker where access to CMR is constrained.

title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Shoulder Pseudodislocation Secondary to Calcific Tendinopathy: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Shoulder pseudodislocation is a rare clinical condition. Imaging examination shows displacement of the humeral head relative to the glenoid, while the osseous anatomical alignment of the joint remains intact. This article reports a 52-year-old female patient with a long history of rotator cuff calcific tendinopathy. The patient presented with recurrent chronic dull shoulder pain, recently aggravated pain, and restricted shoulder movement. Shoulder radiography revealed a dislocation-like appearance of the glenohumeral joint, calcified lesions located at the superolateral humeral head, and widening of the glenohumeral joint space. Given the absence of shoulder trauma, immediate manual reduction was not performed. Further multimodal imaging examinations including CT and MRI were completed, and the patient was finally diagnosed with shoulder pseudodislocation secondary to calcific tendinitis. CT demonstrated calcified deposits at the superolateral humeral head, whereas MRI showed supraspinatus tendon injury, extensive periarticular soft tissue edema, and glenohumeral joint capsular effusion. The patient underwent arthroscopic calcified lesion debridement combined with subacromial decompression. Postoperative radiographic reexamination at day 1 and 2 weeks revealed significant reduction of calcified lesions and gradual recovery of the abnormally widened glenohumeral joint space. Postoperative follow-up showed nearly complete relief of shoulder pain, full recovery of shoulder forward flexion, external rotation and abduction, and unremarkable limitation in daily activities. Based on this rare case, the present study aims to summarize the imaging characteristics and diagnostic and therapeutic strategies of shoulder pseudodislocation secondary to calcific tendinitis, to distinguish soft tissue-induced pseudodislocation from traumatic true shoulder dislocation, and to avoid unnecessary closed reduction. This study provides clinical evidence for preoperative imaging evaluation and minimally invasive surgical treatment of similar rare secondary shoulder lesions.

title: Clinicopathological Features and Prognosis of Acute Interstitial Nephritis: A Study of 26 Patients
abstract: Abstract Objective : Acute interstitial nephritis (AIN) is an acute kidney injury (AKI) characterized by renal interstitial inflammation and tubular damage. This study aims to clarify its clinical features, etiologies, and prognosis. Methods: Clinical data from 26 AIN patients were retrospectively analyzed, including demographics, manifestations, lab tests, ultrasound, pathology, etiology, and outcomes. Results: Mean age was 54.8 years, with 53.8% aged 51–70 years. Females accounted for 61.5% (M:F=1:1.6). Hypertension (42.3%) and diabetes (19.2%) were common comorbidities. Digestive symptoms (38.5%) were the most frequent presentation. AKI occurred in 88.5%, all stage 3, and 38.5% received short-term hemodialysis. Lab findings showed elevated creatinine, BUN, and uric acid, with mild anemia in some. Renal ultrasound revealed increased cortical echogenicity (42.3%) and cysts (23.0%). Biopsy demonstrated interstitial inflammatory infiltration (mainly lymphocytes) in all cases, and 76.9% had interstitial fibrosis. Drug-related causes accounted for 30.8%, while 30.8% remained unknown. Eighteen patients received glucocorticoids. After 3 months, 22 patients were followed up, with a renal recovery rate of 95.5%. Conclusion: AIN is more common in middle-aged and elderly women, with drugs being a major causative factor. It typically presents as severe AKI. Renal biopsy reveals characteristic interstitial inflammation. With active treatment, the overall prognosis is favorable. Emphasis should be placed on preventing and early identifying drug-induced kidney injury.

title: Natural Language Processing and Large Language Model-Based Automated AO/OTA Classification of Proximal Femoral Fractures: A MIMIC-IV Retrospective Study
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate AO/OTA classification of proximal femoral fractures is a critical step in surgical decision-making and prognostic evaluation; however, the complexity of the classification system and the heterogeneity of terminology in radiology reports pose significant challenges for large-scale, standardized application of the classification. In recent years, with the advancement of AI technologies, large language models (LLMs) equipped with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) capabilities have offered new possibilities for automatically extracting fracture classification information from unstructured radiology reports. Methods This study conducted a retrospective analysis of 23,179 radiology reports from the MIMIC-IV database. Through a multi-stage annotation process involving independent labeling by two orthopedic surgeons and adjudication by a senior expert, a total of 157 acute cases of AO/OTA type 31A (intertrochanteric fractures) and type 31B (femoral neck fractures) were ultimately included. We evaluated three experimental models: zero‑shot prompting, few‑shot learning (5 examples per class), and RAG‑augmented prompting (incorporating a structured AO classification knowledge base). Classification performance was assessed using accuracy, F1‑score, and confusion matrices. All type 31C (femoral head fractures) cases underwent expert re‑adjudication to evaluate annotation quality. Results The RAG‑LLM framework achieved an accuracy of 94.29% (F1 = 94.29%) in distinguishing 31A from 31B fractures on a balanced test set of 70 cases (35 each of 31A and 31B). Zero‑shot prompting attained the same accuracy (94.29%, F1 = 94.28%), while few‑shot learning unexpectedly dropped to 88.57% (F1 = 88.53%). Confusion matrices showed minimal misclassifications: 2/35 cases of 31A were misclassified as 31B, and 2/35 cases of 31B were misclassified as 31A. A key finding was that after expert re‑adjudication of 47 cases initially labeled as 31C, only 6 (12.8%) met the true AO/OTA 31C criteria; the remaining 41 (87.2%) were actually acetabular fractures (AO/OTA type 61) or misclassified 31A/31B cases. The subtype classification for 31B fractures (31B1 vs. 31B2) achieved an accuracy of 70.59%, reflecting the inherent difficulty of text‑based subtype differentiation. Conclusion The RAG‑LLM demonstrated excellent performance in binary classification of AO/OTA 31A versus 31B proximal femoral fractures using real‑world radiology reports. The systematic bias found in 31C labeling within MIMIC‑IV highlights the critical importance of expert data quality assurance in real‑world evidence studies. The comparable performance between zero‑shot and RAG models suggests that modern LLMs already possess inherent knowledge of AO/OTA classification, though RAG may offer advantages in more nuanced tasks. These findings support the potential of LLM‑assisted workflows to streamline fracture classification in clinical and research settings.

title: Giant Partially Thrombosed Ophthalmic Segment Internal Carotid Artery Aneurysm With Severe Angiographic–Radiological Discordance: Implications for Microsurgical Strategy
abstract: Abstract Background Giant partially thrombosed aneurysms of the ophthalmic segment of the internal carotid artery (ICA) present substantial diagnostic and therapeutic challenges because intraluminal thrombus and mural calcification can obscure the true aneurysm morphology, leading to underestimation of lesion size on angiography. Methods A 53-year-old man with progressive headache without focal neurological deficits or objective visual impairment underwent multimodal imaging including CT, MRI, CTA, and DSA. The imaging findings were integrated for operative planning, and microsurgical clipping with staged thrombectomy was performed. Results CT and MRI revealed a giant partially thrombosed ophthalmic segment ICA aneurysm compressing the optic apparatus, whereas DSA depicted only a small residual lumen, demonstrating marked angiographic–radiological discordance. Microsurgical clip reconstruction with staged intraluminal thrombectomy achieved complete aneurysm exclusion with preservation of the parent ICA and ophthalmic artery. The patient recovered without new neurological deficits and remained functionally independent at 6-month follow-up. Conclusions Giant partially thrombosed ophthalmic segment ICA aneurysms may be substantially underestimated by DSA alone. Integration of CT, MRI, CTA, and DSA is critical for defining true aneurysm morphology and optimizing skull base microsurgical strategy. Microsurgical reconstruction with staged thrombectomy remains a definitive treatment option in selected patients.

title: MOM-PD: Multimodal Biomarker Optimization for Parkinson's Disease Machine learning-assisted multimodal detection and clinical staging
abstract: Abstract Background: Parkinson's disease (PD) diagnosis relies primarily on clinical motor examination, and the prodromal phase preceding overt motor manifestations remains difficult to identify. No single biomarker modality has been shown to be both sensitive and specific across the full disease spectrum, and how best to integrate multimodal data for stage-specific detection is unclear. Objective: To optimize a multimodal biomarker framework using machine learning based on Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) data, and to define stage-specific biomarkerpanels for manifest PD detection, prodromal identification, and longitudinal progression monitoring. Methods: We analyzed 948 PPMI participants (445 PD, 389 prodromal, 111 healthy controls [HC], 3 SWEDD) with 18 candidate biomarkers spanning dopamine transporter SPECT (DaTscanSBR), structural MRI (FreeSurfer 7 cortical and subcortical metrics), diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and MDS-UPDRS Parts I–IV. Feature-wide association analysis with Mann-Whitney U tests and Cohen's d was followed by random forest Gini importance ranking. Random forest classifiers (500 trees, 5-fold stratified cross-validation) were trained on three feature sets: (1) DaTscan + clinical; (2) structural MRI only; (3) full multimodal combination. Four-year longitudinal trajectories (BL, V06, V10) of motor scores and grey matter volume were characterized. Results: For PD vs HC, the DaTscan-clinical model achieved near-perfect discrimination (AUC = 0.999, 95% CI 0.997–1.000), far exceeding structural MRI alone (AUC = 0.526). Top discriminative features were putaminal SBR, striatal SBR, and MDS-UPDRS Part III motor score. Prodromal vs HC discrimination was more challenging (AUC = 0.700), with subcortical grey matteratrophy as the leading signal while DaTscan SBR was non-discriminative (P = 0.43). PD vs prodromal classification was excellent (AUC = 0.984). Longitudinally, PD motor scores increased ~1.5 points/year and grey matter volume declined ~0.85%/year. Conclusions: Multimodal biomarkers display staging-dependent complementarity: DaTscan and motor scales dominate manifest PD identification, while subcortical volumetric MRI enablesprodromal detection. Stage-tailored biomarker panels support improved PD phenotyping and early screening for clinical trial enrichment.

title: Guidewire coating embolization to the pulmonary artery induced by puncture needle shear injury during cardiac radiofrequency ablation: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Hydrophilic-coated guidewires are essential tools in cardiac interventional procedures. Shear-induced detachment of the hydrophilic coating by a puncture needle represents a rare but potentially serious iatrogenic complication, as dislodged polymer fragments may embolize distally, leading to thrombosis, inflammatory responses, or pulmonary embolism. We present a case of hydrophilic guidewire coating embolization to the pulmonary artery resulting from shear injury by a puncture needle during radiofrequency catheter ablation for a left-sided accessory pathway. Case presentation: A 52-year-old woman with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome underwent radiofrequency catheter ablation. During the procedure, the hydrophilic coating of a guidewire was mechanically stripped by an 18-gauge beveled puncture needle. Fluoroscopy raised suspicion of an intravascular foreign body, and intraoperative cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) precisely localized two thin, loop-like coating fragments, approximately 6 cm and 3 cm in length, within branches of the right inferior pulmonary artery. The three-dimensional spatial information provided by CBCT directly guided the subsequent percutaneous snare retrieval. Both fragments were successfully retrieved via a minimally invasive percutaneous approach using a goose-neck snare. The patient remained asymptomatic throughout the hospital course, with no procedure-related complications, and was discharged on postoperative day 4. At 3-month follow-up, she continued to be symptom-free. Conclusion Percutaneous snare retrieval is an effective intervention for managing hydrophilic guidewire coating embolization to the pulmonary artery. Increased awareness of this complication, avoidance of withdrawing coated guidewires through metallic needles, routine inspection of device integrity, and intraoperative fluoroscopic monitoring are key preventive strategies.

title: Prediction of Lymph Node Metastasis Risk in Endometrial Cancer Using Multi-Sequence Magnetic Resonance Imaging Combined with Deep Transfer Learning
abstract: Abstract Purpose: To develop and externally validate a nomogram integrating clinical predictors, multisequence magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics, and deep learning (DL) features for preoperative lymph node metastasis (LNM) prediction in endometrial cancer (EC), and assess the incremental value of DL. Methods: This two-center retrospective study included 520 patients: 268 for training, 117 for held-out internal validation, and 135 for external validation. Radiomics features were extracted from four MRI sequences, and DL features from four ImageNet-pretrained 50-layer residual network (ResNet-50) branches fine-tuned in training. The Clinical+Radiomics model combined four clinical predictors with a radiomics signature; the nomogram additionally incorporated the DL signature. Final models were fitted using all training patients and evaluated unchanged in both validation cohorts. Assessments included DeLong tests, calibration, decision curve analysis, and prespecified sensitivity analysis in magnetic resonance (MR) report-based LNM-negative patients. Results: In internal and external validation, respectively, the nomogram achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.866 and 0.886, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of 0.786–0.946 and 0.817–0.955. Corresponding Clinical+Radiomics AUCs were 0.733 (95% CI: 0.591–0.875) and 0.715 (95% CI: 0.594–0.836), favoring the nomogram ( P =0.024 and P <0.001, respectively). Brier scores were 0.110 and 0.083. Decision curves favored the nomogram over comparators at probability thresholds of 0.02–0.39 and 0.01–0.71, respectively. Nomogram AUCs in MR report-based LNM-negative subgroups were 0.843 and 0.858, respectively. Conclusion: Adding DL improved discrimination beyond Clinical+Radiomics. The nomogram may complement preoperative LNM risk stratification but should not replace pathological nodal staging. Prospective multicenter validation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Molecular landscape of medullary nephrocalcinosis in children – a nationwide, prospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background This study aimed to investigate the genetic landscape and to identify predictors of a molecular diagnosis in pediatric nephrocalcinosis. Methods This prospective, nationwide cohort study enrolled 79 unrelated pediatric patients with ultrasound-based medullary nephrocalcinosis of unknown etiology. Genetic evaluation was conducted using whole-exome sequencing ( n = 75) or targeted (Sanger) sequencing ( n = 4). Only (likely)pathogenic variants were considered diagnostic. Results A molecular diagnosis of Mendelian disease (MD) was established in 16% of patients, which included infantile hypercalcemia type 1 ( CYP24A1 , n = 3) and type 2 ( SLC34A1 , n = 2), familial hypomagnesemia, hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis ( CLDN16 , n = 2; CLDN19 , n = 1), distal renal tubular acidosis ( ATP6V0A4 , n = 1; ATP6V1B1 , n = 1), Bartter syndrome type 2 ( KCNJ1 , n = 1) and type 3 ( CLCNKB , n = 1), and Dent disease type 1 ( CLCN5 , n = 1). Monoallelic (MA) variants, possibly predisposing to nephrocalcinosis, were found in 16% of patients, encompassing four genes, predominantly within the SLC34A1 and SLC34A3 (61%). In patients with MD, except for two patients with Bartter syndrome, typical phenotypes were observed, in contrast to carriers of MA variants, in whom the majority had subtle abnormalities. Clinical parameters, prematurity and family history for nephrocalcinosis/lithiasis were not associated with MD diagnoses. Conclusions This study clarifies the distinct genetic architecture of pediatric nephrocalcinosis. The data may possibly explain the etiology in approximately 30% of cases, when considering both MD and MA variants. Disease-specific phenotypes are associated with MD; however, the absence of typical features should not preclude a genetic diagnosis.

title: Histopathological Profile of Tobacco-Associated Oral Mucosal Lesions in Chronic Cigarette Smokers: A Five-Year Retrospective Study from a Tertiary Care Centre in Pakistan
abstract: Abstract Background Tobacco smoking has been recognised as one of the key risk factors associated with a wide spectrum of oral mucosal alterations, ranging from benign reactive changes and epithelial dysplasia to malignant oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). Hence, in a population with high tobacco exposure, histopathological assessment remains central to characterise and diagnose potentially malignant and malignant disorders. Objective To evaluate the histopathological profile of tobacco-induced oral mucosal lesions among chronic cigarette smokers and to determine the incidence and degree of epithelial dysplasia and other smoking-associated histological alterations. Methods A retrospective cross-sectional study was carried out in the Department of Histopathology, Ziauddin University Hospital, Karachi, Pakistan. Histopathologically verified oral mucosal biopsy specimens obtained from chronic cigarette smokers from January 2020 to January 2026 were analysed. Information regarding demographics, smoking status, and clinical and histopathological data was derived from archived records. Hematoxylin and eosin-stained microscopic sections were used to study epithelial and stromal changes; epithelial dysplasia was classified according to World Health Organisation criteria. SPSS version 26.0 was used to analyse the data. Results The study was based on 50 oral mucosal biopsy specimens. The study population showed male dominance, with a mean age of 51.79 ± 13.39 years. Buccal mucosa was the most commonly affected anatomical site, while moderately differentiated infiltrative OSCC was the prominent histopathological diagnosis detected in 12 cases (24%). 50% of dysplastic lesions were mild, whereas moderate and severe lesions each accounted for 25%. Conclusion Chronic smoking was linked with a broad range of histopathological alterations in the oral mucosa. A substantial number of cases showed epithelial dysplasia and invasive OSCC. For those with long term use of tobacco, early detection and timely biopsy with histopathological analysis are crucial to identify potential malignant lesions and assess their development. Study findings may help optimise screening and preventive strategies for tobacco-attributed oral cancer in susceptible populations.

title: 18F-FET-PET/MRI versus Standard MRI for Radiotherapy Planning in High-Grade Brain Glioma: A Pilot Study (FETSMaRT)
abstract: Abstract Purpose High-grade gliomas carry a poor prognosis, and MRI-based radiotherapy (RT) planning may inadequately capture metabolically active tumor infiltration. ¹⁸F-fluoroethyl-tyrosine (FET) PET provides superior tumor delineation, yet prospective North American evidence supporting integration with RT planning remains limited. Methods FETSMaRT enrolled 30 patients with WHO grade 3 or 4 high-grade glioma receiving post-operative RT. FET-PET/MRI was acquired before RT with the radiation oncologist blinded to PET, enabling retrospective quantification of discordance between MRI-based and FET-PET/MRI-derived gross tumor (GTV), clinical target (CTV), and planning target (PTV) volumes. In the glioblastoma subgroup (n = 23), Kaplan–Meier and Cox analyses related GTV and CTV discordance to time to progression. Results Median age was 60 years; 77% had glioblastoma and 60% MGMT promoter methylation. GTV discordance occurred in 17/30 patients (56.7%) and CTV discordance in 15/30 (50.0%). FET-PET/MRI-derived volumes significantly exceeded MRI-based volumes for GTV (43.6 vs 38.6 cc; p < 0.0001), CTV (119.2 vs 110.8 cc; p = 0.0045), and PTV (171.1 vs 159.6 cc; p = 0.0003). Larger GTV∆ and CTV∆ change values were associated with numerically shorter median time to progression, but neither association was statistically significant. Radiation treatment failures were predominantly central (60.0%). Conclusion FET-PET/MRI-derived target volumes were significantly larger than MRI-based volumes, confirming systematic underestimation of metabolically active tumor extent by anatomical MRI. While not meeting significance in this pilot study, directional CTV and GTV discordance suggests a possible association with progression; these exploratory pilot data nonetheless justify a prospective trial of FET-PET-guided RT in high-grade glioma. NCT06499831

title: Application of 3D Ultrasound Imaging in School-based Screening for Scoliosis: A Prospective Cross-sectional Study
abstract: Abstract Purpose To investigate the feasibility and efficacy of 3D ultrasound imaging for large-scale school-based scoliosis screening Methods This cross-sectional study screened 9,128 students using a three-stage protocol: (1) Adams test with scoliometer (ATR > 5° as positive); (2) 3D ultrasound imaging with an ultrasound curvature angle (UCA) > 8° for referral and UCA ≥ 10°as the optimal diagnostic threshold via ROC analysis; and (3) whole-spine X-ray as the gold standard (Cobb angle ≥ 10°). Agreement between ultrasound and X-ray measurements was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis and Pearson correlation. Diagnostic performance was evaluated with confirmed scoliosis defined as a radiographic Cobb angle ≥ 10°. Results Among 132 positive initial screenings, 98 underwent ultrasound and 67 had confirmed scoliosis (screen-detected prevalence of 0.73%). Mean UCA was 12.53°±4.15° and Cobb angle was 13.55°±6.11°. Bland-Altman analysis showed a mean bias of -1.02° (95% LoA − 7.46° to 5.42°), with strong Pearson correlation (r = 0.91, p < 0.001; R² = 0.82). Among the 98 referred students, using UCA ≥ 10° as the threshold against X-ray-confirmed Cobb angle ≥ 10°, sensitivity was 89.5%, specificity 58.1%, accuracy 79.6%, PPV 82.2%, and NPV 72.0%. Conclusions This large population-based study confirms that 3D ultrasound serves as a feasible, radiation-free intermediate triage tool for school scoliosis screening. Our three-stage protocol preserves high sensitivity while cutting X-ray referrals by 25.8%. This tiered workflow minimizes unnecessary radiation exposure and optimizes healthcare resource use; refinements to referral thresholds and operator training may lower false-positive rates.

title: The Role of Bronchoscopy pada Acute Lung Atelectasis Due to Airway Mucus Plugging: A Case report
abstract: Abstract Background: Acute lung atelectasis caused by airway mucus plugging is a potentially reversible cause of respiratory failure, particularly in postoperative and critically ill patients. Prompt recognition and timely intervention are essential to prevent prolonged hypoxemia, mechanical ventilation, and other serious complications. Flexible bronchoscopy is considered the gold standard for diagnosing and treating obstructive atelectasis by directly identifying and removing airway obstruction. Case Presentation: A 32-year-old man developed severe hypoxemia and complete right lung atelectasis on the second day following exploratory laparotomy for abdominal trauma. Despite chest tube insertion, invasive mechanical ventilation, and supportive management, oxygenation remained critically impaired. Bedside lung ultrasonography demonstrated extensive right lung collapse. Therapeutic flexible bronchoscopy revealed complete obstruction of the right upper lobe bronchus by a thick mucus plug, with additional retained secretions in the right bronchial tree. Bronchial toilet and suctioning successfully restored airway patency. Immediate post-procedure chest radiography demonstrated significant right lung re-expansion, while arterial oxygenation improved markedly, with PaO₂ increasing from 40 mmHg to 194 mmHg. The patient was subsequently weaned from mechanical ventilation, experienced progressive clinical recovery, and was discharged from the intensive care unit in stable condition. Conclusion: This case highlights that mucus plug-induced atelectasis should be considered in postoperative patients presenting with sudden hypoxemia and radiographic evidence of lung collapse. Early therapeutic flexible bronchoscopy provides both definitive diagnosis and effective treatment by restoring airway patency, promoting rapid lung re-expansion, improving oxygenation, facilitating ventilator weaning, and optimizing clinical outcomes when conservative management is unsuccessful.

Early therapeutic flexible bronchoscopy provides both definitive diagnosis and effective treatment by restoring airway patency, promoting rapid lung re-expansion, improving oxygenation, facilitating ventilator weaning, and optimizing clinical outcomes when conservative management is unsuccessful.

title: Emphysematous Osteomyelitis of the Lumbar Spine Masked by a Urinary Tract Infection in a Diabetic Patient: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Emphysematous osteomyelitis (EO) is a rare and aggressive gas-forming bone infection, most commonly affecting diabetic or immunocompromised patients, with the vertebrae, pelvis, and femur being frequently involved sites. It is most often caused by Klebsiella pneumoniae or Escherichia coli via hematogenous spread, and because of its rarity, its diagnosis is frequently overlooked. Case Presentation: We report the case of a 50-year-old diabetic and hypertensive female who presented with dysuria and dull lower back pain, initially managed as a routine UTI with antibiotics and adjustment of her diabetic regimen. When her urinary symptoms failed to resolve, contrast-enhanced CT of the kidneys, ureters, and bladder incidentally revealed emphysematous osteomyelitis of the L3-L4 vertebrae, with urine culture growing Klebsiella species. Despite targeted intravenous antibiotic therapy (meropenem), her clinical response was poor, necessitating anterior corpectomy with cage reconstruction. Her postoperative course was complicated by severe pain and poorly controlled diabetes, and she subsequently died of cardiopulmonary arrest. Conclusion: This case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for emphysematous osteomyelitis in diabetic patients presenting with back pain, as delayed diagnosis in an immunocompromised host can culminate in a fatal outcome despite aggressive medical and surgical management.

title: Automated Brachial Plexus Localization in Ultrasound Using Lightweight Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Abstract Purpose: Accurate localization of the brachial plexus in ultrasound images is critical for regional anesthesia and perioperative care. Traditional manual interpretation is time-consuming and operator-dependent, while segmentation-based deep learning models, though precise, often demand substantial computational resources, limiting deployment in resource-constrained settings. This study evaluated lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures for automated classification of brachial plexus nerve location into four anatomical quadrants, balancing predictive performance with computational efficiency for point-of-care (POC) environments. Methods: B-mode ultrasound images from the Kaggle Ultrasound Nerve Segmentation dataset were transformed from segmentation masks into a five-class classification task. Three CNN backbones—ResNet34, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNetB0—were trained using 3-fold cross-validation. Data augmentation and class-balancing strategies were applied. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, confusion matrices, and pairwise statistical testing. Results All three models achieved comparable overall performance, with mean accuracies ranging from 0.7288 to 0.7320 and macro-averaged F1-scores from 0.7333 to 0.7365. ResNet34 had the highest mean accuracy and F1-score, though differences between architectures were not statistically significant. Per-class analysis revealed strong performance for majority classes (0 and 2) and lower precision and F1-scores for minority classes, particularly class 3. MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetB0 demonstrated high computational efficiency suitable for on-device deployment. Conclusion Lightweight CNN backbones provide reliable performance for brachial plexus quadrant classification in ultrasound images. While ResNet34 offered marginally higher accuracy, MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetB0 provided better suitability for POC deployment due to lower computational requirements. Future work should address class imbalance and expand evaluation to larger, more diverse datasets.

title: A tunable Synthetic Vascularized Eye Fundus for patient-free retinal imaging validation
abstract: Abstract The validation of novel retinal imaging techniques and motion-correction algorithms is often constrained by biological variability and the lack of ground-truth data in \textit{in vivo} measurements. To address this limitation, patient-free validation platforms require standardized targets that mimic selected optical and structural properties of the human eye. Here, we present a Synthetic Vascularized Eye Fundus (SVEF), a perfusable and contrast-tunable microfluidic insert designed for ophthalmic eye phantom platforms. The SVEF features a high-density, retinal-like vascular network fabricated by soft lithography using a custom polydimethylsiloxane-zinc oxide (PDMS--ZnO) composite. This substrate acts as a bright, diffusely scattering background, while perfusion with hemoglobin solutions generates physiologically relevant absorbing vessel-like structures. By optimizing the hemoglobin concentration, we achieved a vessel-to-background contrast closely matching that of \textit{in vivo} human fundus images. We validated the SVEF as a robust structural reference for image registration, demonstrating accurate retrieval of imposed saccade-like micro-displacements and enabling the enhancement of multi-frame fluorescence imaging. Finally, we confirmed the compatibility of the device with biological assays by successfully integrating and imaging human iPSC-derived retinal neurons. The SVEF provides a reproducible, patient-free environment for benchmarking ophthalmoscopic systems, optimizing image-registration pipelines and supporting versatile \textit{in vitro} retinal experiments.

title: Myxoid Onychomatricoma with Unusual CD99 Expression: A Report of a Rare Case and Literature Review.
abstract: Onychomatricoma (OM) is a rare, benign fibroepithelial tumor originating from the nail matrix, with different clinical and histological variants documented in existing studies. Myxoid OM is an even rarer subtype, characterized by a prominent fibromyxoid component in histopathology. We report a case of a 34-year-old male patient presenting with clinical manifestations consistent with typical OM. Histopathological examination revealed a biphasic tumor composed of an epithelial component and a prominent myxoid stroma, suggesting a diagnosis of myxoid OM. Notably, the tumor exhibited diffuse CD99 positivity, an extremely rare finding in OM. Histopathologically, myxoid OM shows considerable morphological overlap with superficial acral fibromyxoma (SAFM). Our case illustrates that CD99 positivity cannot serve as an absolute criterion to exclude OM; cautious interpretation of this marker is required to avoid diagnostic pitfalls in the differential diagnosis of these two entities. This case expands the immunophenotypic spectrum of myxoid OM and offers a valuable reference for its differential diagnosis. Furthermore, we include and provide a descriptive review to summarize the clinicopathological features and key differential diagnostic considerations of OM, with a focus on diagnostic pitfalls arising from rare histological variants and atypical immunophenotypes, to facilitate accurate differential diagnosis of subungual tumors.

title: Male Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Rare Case of Multisystem Involvement.
abstract: Background Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic autoimmune disease with diverse clinical manifestations. Although SLE predominantly affects women, male patients may present atypically, leading to diagnostic challenges and delays in treatment. Neuropsychiatric involvement and lupus nephritis represent severe manifestations associated with increased morbidity. Case presentation A 31-year-old man presented with fatigue, joint pain, fever, and a photosensitive skin rash. Laboratory investigations showed positive antinuclear antibodies and elevated anti-double-stranded DNA levels. Brain MRI demonstrated scattered T2-weighted and FLAIR hyperintensities suggestive of central nervous system vasculitis, while renal biopsy confirmed class IV lupus nephritis. The patient was treated with corticosteroids, hydroxychloroquine, and mycophenolate mofetil. Follow-up MRI and MRA performed after three weeks showed partial resolution of white matter lesions with stable vasculature. Clinical symptoms improved, and renal function stabilised. Conclusion This case highlights the importance of considering neuropsychiatric SLE in male patients presenting with neurological symptoms and multisystem involvement. MRI and MRA can play an important role in detecting central nervous system involvement and monitoring treatment response, while early recognition and prompt treatment may help prevent irreversible neurological complications.

title: Isolated Ovarian Tuberculosis Mimicking Ovarian Malignancy in a Young Female with Primary Infertility: A Case Report.
abstract: Background Tuberculosis (TB) is an infectious disease that most commonly affects the lungs and remains among the top 10 causes of death worldwide. Isolated ovarian tuberculosis is a rare form of extrapulmonary TB that usually presents with atypical symptoms and infertility. It brings significant diagnostic challenges and may mimic ovarian malignancy. Case presentation A 23-year-old nulliparous Afghan woman underwent laparotomy for suspected ovarian adnexal masses/ovarian tumor after presenting with pelvic pain, prolonged low-grade fever, and infertility for five years following marriage. Intraoperatively, bilateral ovarian cysts were noted; subsequently, bilateral cystectomies were done. Postoperative Histopathology of surgical specimens confirmed the diagnosis of tuberculosis lesions, and the patient was referred for anti-tuberculous therapy. Conclusion Isolated ovarian tuberculosis can present as adnexal masses with elevated CA-125 and could closely mimic ovarian malignancy. This case highlights the need to consider ovarian tuberculosis in the differential diagnosis, particularly in endemic regions. It emphasizes the value of histopathological confirmation to prevent misdiagnosis and to recommend early initiation of antitubercular therapy for favorable clinical outcomes.

title: RECNN-CGAN: A Resource-Efficient Deep Learning Framework for Multi-Class Mammogram Classification and Diagnosis.
abstract: Objective A resource-efficient convolutional neural network with conditional generative adversarial networks (RECNN-CGAN) is proposed for mammogram classification and diagnosis (MCD) to achieve accurate and computationally efficient breast cancer diagnosis. Methods The system employs Gaussian filtering for noise removal, while the Non-Subsampled Contourlet Transform (NSCT) extracts discriminative features from mammograms at multiple scales, preserving directional information. Handcrafted mammographic features are fused with deep representations learned by the proposed dual-branch RECNN, which incorporates a lightweight pooling-integrator mechanism to reduce model complexity while retaining discriminative capability. This design addresses the computational complexity associated with conventional CNNbased mammography classifiers. To address class imbalance and reduce overfitting, the CGAN module generates effective representations of abnormal mammograms. The CGAN module was incorporated to enhance the robustness and generalization of our model. Experiments were performed on three heterogeneous datasets: DDSM (2,620 images), MIAS (325 images), and a private clinical dataset collected from Bharat Scans, Chennai, India, between July 2022 and January 2023 (488 images), encompassing variations in patient characteristics and imaging conditions. Results The proposed model achieved per-class sensitivities of 99.11%, 99.61%, and 99.05%, and specificities of 99.09%, 99.55%, and 99.00% for normal, benign, and cancerous classes, respectively. The accuracy values for the normal, benign, and cancerous cases were 99.06%, 99.47%, and98.95%, respectively. The macro-averaged sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, precision, and F1-score were 99.57%, 99.32%, 99.41%, 98.72%, and 98.75%, respectively. The segmentation component achieved an IoU of 0.982, indicating strong agreement with boundary-level expert annotations. Discussion Dataset-wise per-class evaluation on independent non-augmented test subsets revealed detection rates for the cancerous class to be consistently high across all datasets, thereby minimizing false negatives and false positives, which are critical for early diagnosis and clinical reliability in breast cancer detection. Conclusion Overall, the RECNN-CGAN framework demonstrated superior performance compared with the selected comparative methods, including multitask GCN, ResNet50 + InceptionV3, and CNN-based feature selection approaches, while maintaining lower computational requirements. With diagnostic accuracy, resource efficiency, and robustness across datasets, the proposed system retains a strong chance of integration into large-scale breast cancer screening workflows, particularly when implemented in low-resource or high-throughput clinical settings.

title: Frontal Lobe Metastasis from Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: Papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) is the most common type of well-differentiated thyroid cancer and usually has a favorable prognosis with a low risk of metastasis. However, distant metastasis significantly worsens the prognosis. Brain metastasis of papillary thyroid carcinoma is very rare, and there is currently no standardized treatment protocol for this condition. Case Presentation: A 56-year-old woman was admitted to our hospital 7 years after undergoing total thyroidectomy for primary papillary thyroid carcinoma, presenting with neurological symptoms including decreased mental responsiveness, memory impairment, and motor aphasia. Brain MRI revealed an abnormal mass in the left frontal lobe with extensive surrounding edema. The patient underwent left fronto-temporal craniotomy with complete tumor resection. Postoperatively, the patient showed significant neurological improvement and was started on oral thyroxine replacement therapy. Innovation and Significance: This case provides several noteworthy contributions: (1) It is one of the few reported cases of a single frontal lobe metastatic lesion occurring more than 7 years after primary tumor treatment; (2) It establishes a standardized approach to comprehensive pre- and postoperative neurological assessments; (3) It challenges the traditional view that brain metastases in PTC are almost always associated with extensive systemic dissemination; (4) It provides detailed immunohistochemical characterization of both the primary tumor and the metastatic site. Conclusion: PTC is the most common type of thyroid cancer, typically slow-growing with generally favorable outcomes. Metastases most commonly involve regional lymph nodes, with occasional distant metastases to the lungs and bones. Brain metastases from PTC are extremely rare. In this paper, we present a case of pathologically confirmed PTC brain metastasis in the left frontal lobe and review the available literature on its clinical significance.

title: Effects of Dental Metal Implant Number and Configuration on PET/CT Quantification and Image Quality: A Phantom-Based Study.
abstract: Introduction/objectives Dental metal implants can generate artifacts in PET/CT imaging, particularly in the head and neck region, affecting quantitative accuracy. This study evaluated variations in standardized uptake value (SUV), contrast (C), and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) across predefined dental implant configurations differing in both implant number and spatial arrangement and assessed their effects on simulated tongue, nasopharyngeal, and laryngeal lesions. Methods A custom-designed head and neck phantom containing extracted human teeth and up to eight titanium dental implants was used. Simulated tongue, nasopharyngeal, and laryngeal tumors were filled with F-18 FDG. PET/CT scans were acquired using seven implant configurations (0-8 implants) and reconstructed as attenuation-corrected (AC), AC with metal artifact reduction (AC+MAR), and non-attenuation-corrected (NoAC) images. SUV, contrast, and CNR were calculated using standardized ROIs. Results Compared with the implant-free configuration, tongue tumor SUV decreased by 11% and 9.1% on AC and AC+MAR images, respectively, at eight implants. Nasopharyngeal and laryngeal SUV showed only minimal descriptive change with increasing implant number and configurations on AC+MAR images. Contrast and CNR followed similar trends on AC and AC+MAR images, whereas NoAC images consistently showed substantially lower contrast and CNR regardless of implant number. Discussion Although MAR reduced implant-induced artifacts and partially attenuated SUV underestimation, it did not eliminate the configuration-dependent trend observed across the predefined implant arrangements. Lesions farther from the implants appeared less affected after MAR; however, this should be regarded as a hypothesis-generating observation from a single phantom experiment, requiring validation in patient studies and phantom models with varying implant-to-lesion distances. Conclusion Dental implants may affect PET/CT quantification, particularly for lesions adjacent to multiple implants; SUV measurements in these regions should be interpreted with caution.
originalAbstract:
Introduction/objectives

Dental metal implants can generate artifacts in PET/CT imaging, particularly in the head and neck region, affecting quantitative accuracy. This study evaluated variations in standardized uptake value (SUV), contrast (C), and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) across predefined dental implant configurations differing in both implant number and spatial arrangement and assessed their effects on simulated tongue, nasopharyngeal, and laryngeal lesions.

Methods

A custom-designed head and neck phantom containing extracted human teeth and up to eight titanium dental implants was used. Simulated tongue, nasopharyngeal, and laryngeal tumors were filled with F-18 FDG. PET/CT scans were acquired using seven implant configurations (0-8 implants) and reconstructed as attenuation-corrected (AC), AC with metal artifact reduction (AC+MAR), and non-attenuation-corrected (NoAC) images. SUV, contrast, and CNR were calculated using standardized ROIs.

Results

Compared with the implant-free configuration, tongue tumor SUV decreased by 11% and 9.1% on AC and AC+MAR images, respectively, at eight implants. Nasopharyngeal and laryngeal SUV showed only minimal descriptive change with increasing implant number and configurations on AC+MAR images. Contrast and CNR followed similar trends on AC and AC+MAR images, whereas NoAC images consistently showed substantially lower contrast and CNR regardless of implant number.

Discussion

Although MAR reduced implant-induced artifacts and partially attenuated SUV underestimation, it did not eliminate the configuration-dependent trend observed across the predefined implant arrangements. Lesions farther from the implants appeared less affected after MAR; however, this should be regarded as a hypothesis-generating observation from a single phantom experiment, requiring validation in patient studies and phantom models with varying implant-to-lesion distances.

Conclusion

Dental implants may affect PET/CT quantification, particularly for lesions adjacent to multiple implants; SUV measurements in these regions should be interpreted with caution.

title: Rapid Musculoskeletal MRI in 2026: Clinical Integration of Deep Learning Reconstruction.
abstract: Advances in MRI hardware and acceleration strategies have enabled substantial reductions in musculoskeletal MRI acquisition times over the past decade. Advanced acceleration techniques have facilitated four- to eightfold acceleration but are often limited by noise amplification and reconstruction artifacts at higher acceleration factors. The clinical introduction of deep learning (DL)-based image reconstruction addresses traditional constraints by improving SNRs, reducing artifacts, and enhancing image quality, thereby enabling higher acceleration factors than previously achievable with conventional reconstruction methods. DL reconstruction and superresolution techniques allow comprehensive musculoskeletal MRI protocols to be performed in less than 10 minutes across a range of applications, field strengths, and vendors. Successful implementation requires consideration of hardware capabilities, anatomic constraints, protocol design, and workflow adaptation to fully realize efficiency gains. In addition to technical factors, operational considerations-including scheduling logistics and infrastructure adjustments-are important to translate scan-time reductions into clinical value. Early validation studies show preserved or improved diagnostic performance of DL-accelerated MRI protocols compared with conventional protocols, supporting their growing integration into clinical practice. Continued technical development and clinical validation will further define the role of DL image reconstruction and potentially facilitate even greater acceleration and efficiency gains.

title: Fibroblast Activation Protein-Directed PET: Expanding FAPI Beyond Cancer.
abstract: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) has gained clinical interest as a target for imaging and therapy in a spectrum of oncologic diseases in recent years. Yet, FAP expression by activated fibroblasts is not specific to the tumor microenvironment but rather shows tight coupling to pathologic tissue remodeling, chronic inflammation, and fibrosis across a broad spectrum of nonmalignant diseases. This linkage provides a compelling biologic rationale for extending FAP-directed imaging beyond oncologic applications. Indeed, across various cardiac (ischemic heart disease, nonischemic cardiomyopathy, valvular pathology), vascular (atherosclerosis, vasculitis, aneurysm), rheumatologic (interstitial lung disease, inflammatory arthritis, IgG4-related disease), and other conditions, emerging data suggest that FAP-directed PET may serve as an imaging biomarker for active tissue remodeling. Nonetheless, the supporting clinical evidence is derived primarily from early-stage studies and remains largely exploratory at present. FAP-targeted therapies (e.g., FAP-targeting radiopharmaceutical therapies and chimeric antigen receptor T-cells) are also being actively explored outside of oncology in preclinical settings. While further investigation remains needed, FAP-directed PET has the potential to become a valuable addition to fibrosis-driven disease monitoring. Within this context, this Special Series Review highlights the current early evidence and future potential of FAP-directed PET across a variety of nononcologic conditions.

title: Incidence and predictors of root resorption after delayed replantation of permanent teeth.
abstract: Root resorption is a common but unpredictable complication after delayed replantation of avulsed permanent teeth. Evidence from real-world settings regarding its long-term incidence and associated clinical factors remains limited. This study aimed to determine the incidence of root resorption and identify clinical factors associated with its occurrence following delayed replantation of permanent teeth in a real-world tertiary care setting. This retrospective cohort study analyzed patients aged 7-30 years who underwent delayed replantation (> 60 min extra-alveolar time) between 2019 and 2022 at a tertiary dental trauma center, with ≥ 12 months of follow-up. Clinical and radiographic data were reviewed, and root resorption was classified according to predefined radiographic and clinical criteria. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with the occurrence of root resorption, while Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression were performed to evaluate the time to first root resorption event. Competing-risk analysis was conducted, considering tooth extraction as a competing event. Among 120 eligible patients (mean age 14 ± 5 years), root resorption occurred in 72 teeth (60.0%), including inflammatory (41.7%) and replacement (58.3%) types based on radiographic and clinical classification. Among all delayed replanted teeth, the estimated tooth survival and functional retention rates at 24 months were 78.3% and 68.3%, respectively. Teeth with root resorption showed longer extra-alveolar times, more frequent dry storage, and delayed or absent root canal treatment (all P < 0.01). Multivariable logistic regression identified prolonged extra-alveolar time (> 2 h), dry storage, absence of root canal treatment, and delayed endodontic intervention (> 14 days) as factors associated with a higher occurrence of root resorption. Multivariable logistic regression identified prolonged extra-alveolar time (> 2 h), dry storage, absence of root canal treatment, and delayed endodontic intervention (> 14 days) as factors independently associated with a higher occurrence of root resorption. Root resorption occurred in 60% of delayed replanted teeth in this cohort. Prolonged extra-alveolar time, dry storage, and delayed or absent endodontic treatment were independently associated with a higher occurrence of root resorption. These findings highlight the importance of timely management and appropriate endodontic intervention after delayed replantation; however, the retrospective single-center design limits causal interpretation, and further prospective studies are needed to validate these associations.

title: AI- and Deep Learning-Based Radiomics: A State-of-the-Art Review.
abstract: Radiomics has emerged over the past decade as a powerful image-based omics approach in oncology. Handcrafted radiomic features can reveal subtle imaging characteristics associated with tumor biology and clinical outcomes. In parallel, deep learning (DL) has transformed medical image analysis by learning complex feature representations directly from imaging data. Recent research has increasingly focused on hybrid models that integrate radiomic and DL-derived features to combine the interpretability of radiomics with the representational capacity of DL. Methodological advances have also been made across the radiomics pipeline, including preprocessing, segmentation, feature selection, and machine learning algorithms. This review summarizes current trends in radiomics and hybrid radiomics-DL models applied to CT and MRI, with emphasis on methodological developments in radiomics. It then discusses key challenges, including feature reproducibility and model generalizability, and outlines future directions for developing robust, clinically translatable solutions.

title: Vision-language semantic guidance and topology refinement for robust retinal vessel segmentation and biomarker analysis in cerebral small vessel disease.
abstract: Background Retinal microvascular alterations observed in optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) have emerged as promising biomarkers for cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD). However, accurate quantification of OCTA-derived vascular biomarkers remains challenging due to imaging noise, projection artifacts, low contrast, and structural discontinuities, which often lead to unreliable vessel segmentation and distorted vascular topology. Purpose To address these challenges, we propose SemTopNet, a semantic-topology joint modeling framework for OCTA vessel segmentation. Methods The proposed framework integrates vision-language semantic guidance, centerline-guided topology refinement, and uncertainty-aware adaptive supervision within a unified architecture. Specifically, semantic embeddings are incorporated to enhance global structural representation, while a centerline-guided topology refinement module explicitly improves vascular continuity and suppresses fragmented predictions. In addition, Monte Carlo dropout-based uncertainty estimation is employed to improve robustness in ambiguous and low signal-to-noise regions. Results Extensive experiments on a CSVD OCTA dataset demonstrate that SemTopNet consistently outperforms existing convolutional and Transformer-based segmentation methods, achieving the best performance in Dice similarity coefficient (0.8931), clDice (0.9027), Recall (0.9293), and AUC (0.9567). Ablation studies further verify the effectiveness of semantic modeling, topology-aware refinement, and uncertainty-aware supervision. Based on the obtained segmentation results, quantitative retinal vascular biomarkers were further analyzed, revealing significant layer-dependent microvascular alterations in CSVD patients, particularly in the deep vascular complex (DVC). Conclusion These findings demonstrate that topology-consistent OCTA vessel segmentation is essential for reliable retinal microvascular quantification. The proposed SemTopNet provides a robust framework for OCTA biomarker extraction and retinal-cerebral vascular association analysis in CSVD-related studies.

title: Correlation between myocardial radiomics features at the left atrium-left atrial appendage junction and stroke risk in atrial fibrillation patients: a retrospective case-control study.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to systematically evaluate the microstructure changes of the myocardium at the left atrium-left atrial appendage (LA-LAA) junction in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF)-related cardioembolic stroke, and to explore its potential role as an imaging marker associated with stroke. Methods This retrospective study included four groups: AF-related cardioembolic stroke group ( n = 60), AF-non-stroke group ( n = 29), non-AF-stroke ( n = 53), and non-AF-non-stroke ( n = 53). All subjects underwent cardiac computed tomography examination. Myocardial thickness at the LA-LAA junction was measured, and radiomics features were extracted. Radiomics features included first-order statistical features, shape features, and texture features. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression was used to screen features, and a logistic regression model combining radiomics features and clinical parameters was constructed. Group comparisons were performed using t-tests or Mann-Whitney U tests. The predictive ability of the model was evaluated with the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, and a nomogram was used for risk assessment. Results Compared with AF patients without stroke, patients with AF-related cardioembolic stroke significantly increased myocardial thickness at the LA-LAA junction [7.1 (6.43-8.33) mm vs. 6.58 ± 1.45 mm, p < 0.05]. In addition, multivariate logistic regression demonstrated that myocardial thickness was independently associated with AF-related cardioembolic stroke. Three radiomics features were selected by LASSO regression in AF-related cardioembolic stroke and non-AF-non-stroke patients, and a radiomics score (Rad-score) was generated. The Rad-score was statistically significant between the groups ( p < 0.001). The combined model incorporating Rad-score and clinical parameters achieved an area under curve (AUC) of 0.968 in the test cohort. Conclusion Both myocardial radiomics features and myocardial thickness at the LA-LAA junction may serve as potential imaging markers associated with AF-related cardioembolic stroke. Their incremental value for stroke risk stratification beyond established clinical risk factors requires further validation in larger prospective cohorts.

title: Comparative evaluation of explainable vision models for bone tumour detection on radiographs.
abstract: Introduction Accurate detection of bone tumours on radiographs can be challenging because lesion appearance varies and interpretation requires specialist expertise. This study evaluates deep learning (DL) models for bone tumour localisation, segmentation, classification, and explainability using the publicly available Bone Tumour X-Ray Radiograph Dataset (BTXRD), comprising 3,746 musculoskeletal radiographs. Methods A YOLOv8s-seg model was evaluated alongside MobileNetV3-Large, EfficientNet-B3, and ConvNeXt-Tiny classifiers trained under a common-resolution protocol. Grad-CAM, Grad-CAM++, and Layer-CAM activation maps were compared with expert tumour masks using mean Intersection over Union and a thresholded lesion-overlap measure. For the retrospective agreement analysis, EfficientNet-B3 was paired with YOLOv8s-seg. An exploratory external series of 11 tumour-positive radiographs was also examined. Results ConvNeXt-Tiny achieved the highest binary classification accuracy (0.879), while YOLOv8s-seg achieved an overall box mAP50 of 0.676 and mask mAP50 of 0.668. The components produced concordant binary tumour-presence predictions for 605 of 750 test radiographs, corresponding to 80.7% coverage (95% confidence interval [CI]: 77.7%-83.3%). Binary accuracy within the agreed subset was 93.6% (566/605; 95% CI: 91.3%-95.2%), while the remaining 145 cases were discordant and received no consensus output. Discussion The XAI analyses quantify spatial correspondence rather than explanation faithfulness or clinical reliability. Because the exploratory external series contained seven benign and four malignant tumour-positive radiographs and no normal radiographs, it cannot assess specificity or false-positive behaviour and is not presented as representative external validation.

title: Multimodal endoscopic diagnosis in biliary oncology: integrating EUS-guided tissue acquisition and cholangioscopy for personalized cancer care.
abstract: The diagnosis of biliary malignancies remains challenging because of the heterogeneous growth patterns of cholangiocarcinoma, the limited sensitivity of conventional tissue acquisition techniques, and the growing need for molecular profiling in the era of precision oncology. Over the past decade, endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) and digital single-operator cholangioscopy have transformed the diagnostic approach by providing complementary information. EUS enables high-resolution imaging, locoregional staging, and tissue acquisition from primary tumors and regional lymph nodes, while cholangioscopy offers direct intraductal visualization and targeted biopsy of suspicious biliary lesions. This review summarizes the current evidence on the diagnostic performance, strengths, and limitations of EUS-guided tissue acquisition and cholangioscopy, emphasizing their complementary role within contemporary diagnostic algorithms. We also discuss emerging technologies, including molecular profiling, next-generation sequencing, artificial intelligence, radiomics, digital pathology, and liquid biopsy, which are shaping the future of biliary oncology. In addition to the available evidence, we present our institutional experience comparing EUS-guided tissue acquisition and cholangioscopy-directed biopsy in patients with suspected malignant biliary strictures. Our institutional experience supports the complementary use of EUS-guided tissue acquisition and cholangioscopy within a multimodal diagnostic approach. title: Pretreatment CT radiomics for prediction of pathological complete response after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in NSCLC: a multicenter study incorporating habitat analysis.
abstract: Background Pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NACI) varies among patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This study aimed to quantify intratumoral heterogeneity using habitat analysis and to develop a pretreatment model for predicting pCR. Methods In this retrospective multicenter study, 287 patients with NSCLC who received NACI followed by surgery were included. Patients were randomly divided into a training cohort (n = 147) and an internal validation cohort (n = 63), with an independent external test cohort (n = 77). K-means clustering was used to partition tumors into three habitat subregions based on entropy. Radiomics features were extracted from pretreatment CT images at the whole-tumor and habitat levels. Whole-tumor, habitat-based, and combined models were developed to predict pCR. Model performance was evaluated using area under the curve (AUC) analysis, and model interpretability was assessed using Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results The habitat-based model showed acceptable predictive performance across the training, internal validation, and external test cohorts, with AUCs of 0.74, 0.71, and 0.67, respectively, and showed higher AUCs compared with the whole-tumor radiomics model, which achieved AUCs of 0.72, 0.68, and 0.65. The combined model achieved performance comparable to the habitat-based model. SHAP analysis suggested that, among the habitat-derived features, the most influential predictive features were primarily associated with the high-entropy habitat subregion. Conclusion The habitat-based model shows potential performance for predicting pCR, and features from a high-entropy habitat subregion may provide complementary imaging information for preoperative assessment of treatment response.

title: Regularization via gradient attribution for multiple sclerosis lesion segmentation.
abstract: Introduction Accurate segmentation of Multiple Sclerosis (MS) lesions from Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is fundamental for robust disease monitoring and for the evaluation of therapeutic efficacy. Within Internet of Medical Things (IoMT)-based diagnostic infrastructures, where deep learning models serve as autonomous computational nodes embedded in interconnected clinical workflows, ensuring reliable lesion detection without continuous human supervision is a critical operational and clinical requirement. A persistent methodological challenge is the pronounced class imbalance characteristic of MS neuroimaging datasets. This imbalance causes conventional loss functions to systematically miss small lesions, thereby directly compromising the utility of automated image analysis as an instrument for precision medicine. Methods This work proposes the Regularization via Gradient Attribution (RGA) framework, a module that leverages gradient-based eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) attribution maps as active supervisory signals during training. Instead of constraining the learning process exclusively at the prediction-output level, RGA imposes additional penalties on the network when false-negative lesion regions have low internal attribution and when false-positive healthy-tissue regions exhibit elevated attribution. The framework is architecturally agnostic, compatible with both convolutional and transformer-based backbone networks, and accommodating arbitrary spatial attribution techniques. RGA was evaluated on two public MS lesion segmentation datasets, MSLesSeg and 3D-MR-MS, using three backbones (nnU-Net, UNETR, TransBTS) and two XAI methods (LayerCAM, Integrated Gradients) in 5-fold cross-validation. Results On both datasets, RGA consistently improved DSC, TPR, and LTPR over the baselines. The best configuration, nnU-Net + RGA achieved a DSC of 0.7056 on MSLesSeg and 0.7466 on 3D-MR-MS, with RGA yielding the highest DSC for all backbones. Qualitative analyses further substantiate these findings by demonstrating a marked reduction in missed-lesion regions across all model architectures, without a corresponding substantial increase in false-positive predictions. Discussion By jointly providing high lesion-level detection completeness, model interpretability, and zero additional inference-time computational cost, RGA represents a methodologically grounded approach compatible with IoMT-oriented precision-medicine pipelines, while requiring dedicated deployment validation before clinical or edge-device implementation.

title: Enhanced efficiency and endothelial protection of the intraocular lens shell technique in phacoemulsification: a retrospective stratified analysis by nuclear hardness.
abstract: Background The intraocular lens (IOL)-shell technique may improve intraoperative stability during phacoemulsification, but whether its benefits vary by nuclear hardness remains uncertain. This study evaluated the safety and efficiency of the IOL-shell technique and explored its effects across nuclear hardness subgroups. Methods This retrospective study included 200 patients undergoing phacoemulsification: 100 treated with the IOL-shell technique and 100 treated with the conventional technique. Outcomes included operative time, cumulative dissipated energy (CDE), corneal endothelial cell loss, posterior capsule rupture (PCR), corneal edema, and best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) at 1 month. Subgroup and interaction analyses were performed according to nuclear hardness (≥ Grade IV vs. ≤ Grade III). Results Baseline characteristics were comparable between groups. Compared with the conventional group, the IOL-shell group had shorter operative time (12.79 ± 2.00 vs. 15.13 ± 2.52 min, P < 0.001), lower CDE (8.36 ± 2.05 vs. 12.03 ± 2.78 units, P < 0.001), less endothelial cell loss (10.74 ± 3.55% vs. 14.59% ± 3.95%, P < 0.001), a lower corneal edema rate (18.0% vs. 32.0%, P = 0.022), and better 1-month BCVA (0.29 ± 0.08 vs. 0.36 ± 0.12 logMAR, P < 0.001). PCR was numerically lower with the IOL-shell technique but was not statistically significant overall (2.0% vs. 8.0%, P = 0.101). In eyes with nuclear hardness ≥ Grade IV, the IOL-shell technique was associated with shorter operative time, lower CDE, reduced endothelial cell loss, and lower PCR and corneal edema rates. Interaction analysis showed a significant technique-by-nuclear hardness interaction for operative time ( β = -1.58, 95% CI : -2.93 to -0.23; P for interaction = 0.022), but not for other outcomes. Conclusions The IOL-shell technique improved surgical efficiency, reduced ultrasound energy use, enhanced endothelial protection, decreased corneal edema, and promoted early visual recovery after phacoemulsification. Its efficiency advantage was particularly evident in eyes with nuclear hardness ≥ Grade IV. The apparent reduction in PCR should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of events.

title: Clinical efficacy and neural mechanisms of Tuina for primary dysmenorrhea with cold congestion and blood stasis pattern: a protocol for a randomized controlled fMRI trial.
abstract: Background Primary dysmenorrhea (PD) is one of the most common gynecological disorders in women of reproductive age and significantly impairs quality of life. Epidemiological data indicate that the cold congestion and blood stasis pattern accounts for a large proportion of PD cases. Tuina, a traditional Chinese external therapy, has unique advantages in pain management; however, its clinical efficacy and central mechanisms for PD remain unclear. Objective This study aims to conduct an assessor-blind, parallel-group randomized controlled superiority trial, integrating functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), to evaluate the clinical efficacy, safety, and central brain network modulation of Tuina therapy for primary dysmenorrhea with the cold congestion and blood stasis pattern. Methods This study employed a randomized controlled trial design. A total of 54 patients who met the diagnostic criteria were recruited and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the treatment or control group. An additional 15 healthy women were included as the healthy group. Participants in the treatment group received standardized manipulation over two consecutive menstrual cycles. For each cycle, treatment began 7 days before menstruation and was administered once daily for 7 consecutive days. Participants in the control group received conventional oral ibuprofen, taken as needed for pain relief. The primary outcome was the change in the Visual Analog Scale score. Secondary outcomes included the COX Menstrual Symptom Scale, Traditional Chinese Medicine pattern score, sleep index, and psychological assessments. All outcomes were evaluated at three time points: baseline, after the first treatment cycle, and after the second treatment cycle. All participants underwent two fMRI sessions-both resting-state and task-state fMRI scans-during days 1-3 of their menstrual cycle: once before enrollment and once after the treatment period. All statistical analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle. Discussion This study aims to provide high-level clinical evidence on pain relief, symptom improvement, and brain functional network regulation for the treatment of cold congestion stasis type dysmenorrhea with Tuina therapy, using a randomized controlled trial design combined with functional magnetic resonance imaging. Clinical trial registration https://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn, International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial Registry ITMCTR2026001387.
